# Card 5 step-5 pre-Layer-2 baseline

Security-Datasets commit: `d9d40ef123d2c87d5d3df28c96bcab4f0faccc87`

## Primary strict metrics

Sample-level predictions are compared to metadata ATT&CK IDs using exact IDs. Micro scores aggregate TP/FP/FN across all 40 captures.

|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Current runtime | 0.063 | 0.125 | 0.084 | 5 | 74 | 35 |
| Layer-1 preview | 0.018 | 0.650 | 0.036 | 26 | 1391 | 14 |

## Checkpoint verdict and failure analysis

The Layer-1 preview clears the proposed recall bar (65.0% versus 60%) but fails the proposed precision bar (1.8% versus 80%). It raises recall by +52.5 percentage points from the current runtime, while precision changes by -4.5 percentage points.

The preview emits a mean of 35.4 distinct technique IDs per capture (minimum 15, maximum 77). Parent/sub-technique-family scoring improves the result only to 2.7% precision and 75.0% recall, so ID granularity is not the main cause of the precision failure.

Most frequent strict false-positive technique IDs:

- `T1036` in 40/40 captures
- `T1048.003` in 40/40 captures
- `T1106` in 40/40 captures
- `T1564.004` in 40/40 captures
- `T1574.001` in 40/40 captures
- `T1649` in 40/40 captures
- `T1098` in 39/40 captures
- `T1546.003` in 39/40 captures
- `T1686.003` in 39/40 captures
- `T1200` in 36/40 captures

Most frequent contributing sources (one count per affected capture):

- `Sigma: net_connection_win_susp_outbound_smtp_connections.yml` in 40/40 captures
- `Sigma: proc_creation_win_susp_inline_win_api_access.yml` in 40/40 captures
- `Sigma: win_dns_server_susp_server_level_plugin_dll.yml` in 40/40 captures
- `Sigma: win_capi2_acquire_certificate_private_key.yml` in 40/40 captures
- `Sigma: file_event_win_shell_write_susp_files_extensions.yml` in 39/40 captures
- `Sigma: create_stream_hash_ads_executable.yml` in 39/40 captures
- `Sigma: sysmon_wmi_event_subscription.yml` in 38/40 captures
- `Sigma: win_security_susp_outbound_kerberos_connection.yml` in 36/40 captures
- `Sigma: win_security_audit_log_cleared.yml` in 36/40 captures
- `Sigma: proc_creation_win_lsass_process_clone.yml` in 35/40 captures

The dominant failure is field erasure in the pre-Layer-2 raw-text projection. The generated regexes preserve Boolean structure but not which JSON field a literal belongs to. Representative examples are:

- `sysmon_wmi_event_subscription.yml` becomes an OR of `19`, `20`, and `21`; ordinary timestamp years satisfy it without a matching event ID.
- `win_capi2_acquire_certificate_private_key.yml` becomes the literal `70`; unrelated numeric values satisfy it without a CAPI2 EventID field.
- `win_dns_server_susp_server_level_plugin_dll.yml` becomes an OR of `150`, `770`, and `771`; those numbers can occur anywhere in an event.
- `net_connection_win_susp_outbound_smtp_connections.yml` requires one of `25`, `587`, `465`, or `2525` plus `true`, but no longer binds those values to `DestinationPort` and `Initiated`.

## Method and limitations

- This is the existing raw-text detector/parser/regex approach; no canonical field extraction is used.
- The primary metric is sample-level exact ATT&CK-ID matching. A parent/sub-technique family diagnostic is included in JSON but is not used as the headline result.
- Each capture contains attack activity plus surrounding host telemetry. Predictions outside the metadata labels count as false positives, even when they may describe real secondary behavior present in the capture.
- This attack-only corpus cannot establish a benign-log false-positive rate; that requires the separate benign batch described in Card 5 Layer 3.
- A conservative mandatory-literal prefilter skips lines that cannot satisfy a regex, then the original Python regex decides every candidate. This changes performance, not matching semantics.
- The external fixture is not committed. The pinned LICENSE is MIT, while the pinned README contains a contradictory GPL-3.0 sentence.
